meta.name: Buffett Four-Filters US Equity Screening
meta.description: Parallel research screening of one US equity using Warren Buffett's four filters — circle of competence, durable competitive advantage (moat), able and trustworthy management, and attractive price with margin of safety — plus a modern financial-quality supplement. Each ticker is one row; the cloud runs four parallel reviews; the local Skill applies evidence audit, hard vetos, deterministic ranking, and an auditable Markdown report. Research aid only — not investment advice. The Skill never produces target prices, position sizes, or buy/sell instructions.

presentation.label: Ticker data packet (JSON string)
presentation.description: Three JSON-encoded packets concatenated as one string: identityPacket, financialPacket, qualitativePacket. The local Skill's preflight validates freshness, HTTPS sources, and unit consistency before this template is invoked.

steps.display_name: Business model & circle of competence review

parts.literal:
You are auditing one US equity under Warren Buffett's first filter — Circle of Competence and the underlying business model. Work strictly from the tickerPacket JSON supplied. Every claim must trace back to a field in the packet.

INPUT (tickerPacket JSON):

PACKET SCHEMA (use ONLY these paths in source_ref; the local audit rejects anything not in this schema):

identityPacket: ticker, companyName, industry, dataAsOf, fiscalPeriod, sources (array of URLs)
financialPacket:
  marketSnapshot: price (number), currency (string), asOf (ISO timestamp), pe (number|null)
  annualHistory: fiscalYearEnd (array of YYYY-MM-DD), revenue (array of numbers), netIncome (array of numbers), freeCashFlow (array of numbers) — index by fiscal year position
  quarterlyMostRecent: period, revenue, netIncome, freeCashFlow, unit, source
  unknowns: array of strings
qualitativePacket:
  businessModel, moatEvidence, managementCulture, capitalAllocation, riskFactors, contraryEvidence, unknowns — each is an array of {fact, source, date, sourceType}

PATH RULES (HARD — every evidence entry MUST pass all of these; the local Skill audit will reject any entry that does not):
1. source_ref MUST be one of these two forms:
   (a) '<packetName>.<field>...'  e.g. financialPacket.marketSnapshot.price or qualitativePacket.moatEvidence[0].fact
   (b) '<field>...' (no packet prefix)  e.g. marketSnapshot.price or moatEvidence[0].fact — the local audit resolves this against the packet implied by your dimension (business -> qualitativePacket, moat -> qualitativePacket, financial -> financialPacket, valuation -> financialPacket)
2. NEVER use the 'tickerPacket.' prefix. tickerPacket is the input wrapper that holds the three inner packets; the local audit treats 'tickerPacket.x' as unresolvable.
3. NEVER invent field names. If the field you want to cite is not in the schema above, move the claim to 'unknowns'.
4. For array elements use [index] — e.g. qualitativePacket.riskFactors[2].fact or financialPacket.annualHistory.netIncome[1].
5. source_value MUST be the EXACT, verbatim atomic value at source_ref:
   - string  -> copy character-for-character (whitespace, punctuation, casing included)
   - number  -> the same number, no rounding, no $ sign, no thousand separators, no unit suffix
   - boolean / null -> copy as-is
   - objects / arrays are NOT atomic evidence. If you need to cite a multi-element value, split into multiple atomic entries (one per field) or move the fact to 'unknowns'.
6. period should be either a fiscal-year tag like 'FY2026' or an ISO date like '2026-09-03' matching the date field of the cited fact.

OUTPUT SCHEMA — emit ONLY a single JSON object wrapped in ```json ... ``` fences. No prose outside the fence. Keys and types must match exactly. Missing fields are not allowed.

{
  "dimension": "business",
  "business_model_score": <integer 0-100>,
  "understandability_score": <integer 0-100>,
  "circle_of_competence": <"pass" | "uncertain" | "fail">,
  "summary": "<one-paragraph verdict>",
  "positive_points": ["<atomic fact, not opinion>", ...],
  "contrary_points": ["<atomic fact, not opinion>", ...],
  "unknowns": ["<what you could not verify>", ...],
  "evidence_records": [
    {"claim": "<text>", "source_ref": "<full path like identityPacket.companyName or financialPacket.marketSnapshot.pe>", "source_value": <verbatim value from the packet>, "period": "<FY2025 or YYYY-MM-DD>", "unit": "<USD or text or %>"}
  ]
}

SCORING GUIDE
- business_model_score: 0-100 reflecting durability and clarity of the business model.
- understandability_score: 0-100 for whether a normal investor can explain how the company makes money in one paragraph.
- circle_of_competence: pass if the business is intelligible and inside typical investor understanding; uncertain if it is complex; fail if opaque or off-circle.

DISCIPLINE
- Every source_ref MUST be a complete public path that resolves inside the supplied tickerPacket.
- Every source_value MUST be the exact value at that path. Arrays, objects, and recomputed summaries are NOT atomic evidence.
- DO NOT emit target prices, future share prices, forecast growth, forecast margins, discount rates, terminal multiples, or probabilities. If a field would require such a number, write it as a forbidden_numeric_claim or leave it out.
- If you cannot verify something, write it to unknowns, not to evidence_records.

{
  "dimension": "moat",
  "moat_score": <integer 0-100>,
  "management_culture_score": <integer 0-100>,
  "capital_allocation_score": <integer 0-100>,
  "summary": "<one-paragraph verdict on moat and management>",
  "positive_points": ["<atomic fact>", ...],

  ]
}

SCORING GUIDE
- moat_score: 0-100 for structural pricing power, switching cost, network effect, scale, or brand durability. Buffett's most decisive filter.
- management_culture_score: 0-100 for honesty, competence, owner-mindset, and track record.
- capital_allocation_score: 0-100 for shareholder-friendly buybacks, dividends, M&A discipline, and avoidance of value-destroying acquisitions.

DISCIPLINE
- source_ref MUST be a complete public path resolvable inside the supplied tickerPacket.
- source_value MUST be the exact value at that path. Arrays, objects, and recomputed summaries are NOT atomic evidence.
- governance_red_flags must be specific events (e.g. a restatement, a related-party transaction), not generic risks.
- DO NOT emit target prices, future share prices, forecast growth, forecast margins, discount rates, or terminal multiples. If a field would require such a number, omit it.

You are auditing one US equity's Financial Quality — the modern supplement to Buffett's four filters. Focus on capital returns, free cash flow generation, balance sheet strength, and accounting integrity. Work strictly from the tickerPacket JSON supplied.

identityPacket: ticker, companyName, industry, dataAsOf, fiscalPeriod, sources (array of URLs)

{
  "dimension": "financial",
  "financial_quality_score": <integer 0-100>,

  "summary": "<one-paragraph verdict>",

  ]

SCORING GUIDE
- financial_quality_score: 0-100 for combined ROIC, margin stability, and earnings quality.
- cash_flow_quality_score: 0-100 for free cash flow conversion relative to net income and capex coverage.
- balance_sheet_score: 0-100 for cash to debt, lease obligations vs EBITDA, and shareholder dilution. A score below 30 is treated as 'weak balance sheet' by the local Skill.

- source_ref MUST be a complete public path resolvable inside the supplied tickerPacket.

You are auditing one US equity's Valuation with Margin of Safety — Buffett's fourth filter. Price judgment must bind to a price timestamp AND a fiscal period. Output the validity_basis (one price/time reference and one period reference) and 2-4 falsification conditions, each with a rerun/conclusion_invalidated action. Work strictly from the tickerPacket JSON supplied.

INPUT (tickerPacket JSON):

PACKET SCHEMA (use ONLY these paths in source_ref; the local audit rejects anything not in this schema):

identityPacket: ticker, companyName, industry, dataAsOf, fiscalPeriod, sources (array of URLs)
financialPacket:
  marketSnapshot: price (number), currency (string), asOf (ISO timestamp), pe (number|null)
  annualHistory: fiscalYearEnd (array of YYYY-MM-DD), revenue (array of numbers), netIncome (array of numbers), freeCashFlow (array of numbers) — index by fiscal year position
  quarterlyMostRecent: period, revenue, netIncome, freeCashFlow, unit, source
  unknowns: array of strings
qualitativePacket:
  businessModel, moatEvidence, managementCulture, capitalAllocation, riskFactors, contraryEvidence, unknowns — each is an array of {fact, source, date, sourceType}

PATH RULES (HARD — every evidence entry MUST pass all of these; the local Skill audit will reject any entry that does not):
1. source_ref MUST be one of these two forms:
   (a) '<packetName>.<field>...'  e.g. financialPacket.marketSnapshot.price or qualitativePacket.moatEvidence[0].fact
   (b) '<field>...' (no packet prefix)  e.g. marketSnapshot.price or moatEvidence[0].fact — the local audit resolves this against the packet implied by your dimension (business -> qualitativePacket, moat -> qualitativePacket, financial -> financialPacket, valuation -> financialPacket)
2. NEVER use the 'tickerPacket.' prefix. tickerPacket is the input wrapper that holds the three inner packets; the local audit treats 'tickerPacket.x' as unresolvable.
3. NEVER invent field names. If the field you want to cite is not in the schema above, move the claim to 'unknowns'.
4. For array elements use [index] — e.g. qualitativePacket.riskFactors[2].fact or financialPacket.annualHistory.netIncome[1].
5. source_value MUST be the EXACT, verbatim atomic value at source_ref:
   - string  -> copy character-for-character (whitespace, punctuation, casing included)
   - number  -> the same number, no rounding, no $ sign, no thousand separators, no unit suffix
   - boolean / null -> copy as-is
   - objects / arrays are NOT atomic evidence. If you need to cite a multi-element value, split into multiple atomic entries (one per field) or move the fact to 'unknowns'.
6. period should be either a fiscal-year tag like 'FY2026' or an ISO date like '2026-09-03' matching the date field of the cited fact.

HISTORICAL VALUATION RANGE (NEW in v3) — when the packet does NOT contain explicit normalized owner earnings or a stated historical P/E range, you may anchor margin_of_safety on a publicly observable historical P/E band cited from the issuer's most recent 10-K Item 5 (Market for Registrant's Common Equity — stock performance graph and selected financial data) and the 10-K Item 6 (Selected Financial Data). Cite the source as: 'publicly observable historical P/E band for [ticker] since FY[year], per 10-K Item 5 stock performance graph'. Do not invent a precise number — state the range (e.g. 'JPM has traded 9-15x trailing P/E for most of the last decade'). The local audit accepts this as a qualitative source_ref under qualitativePacket.unknowns; the source_value can be a string range, not a number. Do NOT extrapolate into target prices or forward P/E; report the past band only.

3-TIER MARGIN-OF-SAFETY CALIBRATION (NEW in v3) — choose exactly one judgment_state:
- 'eligible_for_manual_deep_research' — margin_of_safety_score >= 60, both valuation_score and margin_of_safety_score are 60+, no red flag fires, AND you have either (a) explicit normalized owner earnings in the packet, or (b) explicit historical P/E range from a 10-K Item 5 citation.
- 'evidence_thin' — margin_of_safety_score in [30, 60] AND you have current P/E + qualitative moat evidence, but you lack either normalized owner earnings or an explicit historical P/E range from 10-K Item 5. This tier is NOT a veto; the local audit surfaces it as a 'watchlist' decision so a human can manually anchor valuation.
- 'insufficient_margin_of_safety' — current price is meaningfully above the intrinsic value anchor you can defend; margin_of_safety_score < 60 and the price-vs-value gap is the dominant signal.
- 'evidence_insufficient' — you cannot defend ANY valuation anchor (no owner earnings, no historical P/E range, no comparable multiples, no qualitative moat). The packet is too thin to make a price-vs-value judgment. The local audit treats this as a hard veto.

OUTPUT SCHEMA — emit ONLY a single JSON object wrapped in ```json ... ``` fences. No prose outside the fence. Keys and types must match exactly. Missing fields are not allowed.

{
  "dimension": "valuation",
  "valuation_score": <integer 0-100>,
  "margin_of_safety_score": <integer 0-100>,
  "judgment_state": <"insufficient_margin_of_safety" | "evidence_insufficient" | "evidence_thin" | "eligible_for_manual_deep_research">,
  "summary": "<one-paragraph verdict>",
  "positive_points": ["<atomic fact>", ...],
  "contrary_points": ["<atomic fact>", ...],
  "valuation_red_flags": ["<atomic fact>", ...],
  "forbidden_numeric_claims": ["<claim we deliberately avoid making>", ...],
  "unknowns": ["<what you could not verify — and which tier of the 3-tier calibration you are using as a result>", ...],
  "validity_basis": [
    {"claim": "<one binds to price or price timestamp>", "source_ref": "financialPacket.marketSnapshot.price or financialPacket.marketSnapshot.asOf", "source_value": <verbatim value>, "period": "<YYYY-MM-DD>", "unit": "<USD or text>"},
    {"claim": "<one binds to fiscal period or data-as-of date>", "source_ref": "identityPacket.fiscalPeriod or identityPacket.dataAsOf or financialPacket.annualHistory.fiscalYearEnd[0]", "source_value": <verbatim value>, "period": "<FY2025 or YYYY-MM-DD>", "unit": "<text>"}
  ],
  "falsification_conditions": [
    {"condition": "<what new fact would invalidate this verdict>", "source_ref": "<full path>", "source_value": <verbatim value>, "period": "<YYYY-MM-DD or FY2025>", "unit": "<USD or text>", "action": "<rerun_required | conclusion_invalidated>"},
    {"condition": "<second falsifier>", "source_ref": "<full path>", "source_value": <verbatim value>, "period": "<YYYY-MM-DD or FY2025>", "unit": "<USD or text>", "action": "<rerun_required | conclusion_invalidated>"}
  ],
  "evidence_records": [
    {"claim": "<text>", "source_ref": "<full path>", "source_value": <verbatim value>, "period": "<YYYY-MM-DD or FY2025>", "unit": "<USD or %>"}
  ]
}

SCORING GUIDE
- valuation_score: 0-100 for whether the current price is reasonable vs. owner earnings, peer history, and a stated opportunity cost.
- margin_of_safety_score: 0-100 for distance between price and a defensible intrinsic value anchor. A score below 30 triggers a local hard veto regardless of judgment_state.
- judgment_state: see 3-TIER CALIBRATION above. Choose exactly one of the four values; do not default to 'evidence_insufficient' for every packet.

DISCIPLINE
- validity_basis MUST include exactly one price/price-time reference and one period/date reference.
- falsification_conditions MUST each carry a 'rerun_required' or 'conclusion_invalidated' action.
- 'evidence_thin' is preferred over 'evidence_insufficient' when you have ANY defensible anchor (current P/E + qualitative moat, or a 10-K Item 5 historical P/E range). Reserve 'evidence_insufficient' for packets where the issuer is genuinely opaque (e.g. a recent IPO with no public 10-K history, or a ticker the local Agent could not source 3 fiscal years of financials for).
- source_ref MUST be a complete public path resolvable inside the supplied tickerPacket, OR a public-knowledge citation in qualitativePacket.unknowns with a textual range (e.g. '10-K Item 5 historical P/E band 9-15x for JPM since FY2015').
- source_value MUST be the exact value at source_ref for packet-internal paths; for the public-knowledge historical range form, source_value is a string range like '9-15x'.
- DO NOT emit target prices, future share prices, forecast growth, forecast margins, discount rates, terminal multiples, or probabilities. If you feel the urge, write it to forbidden_numeric_claims and move on.

instructions: One US equity per row. Supply a JSON string in tickerPacket containing the three Skill packets: identityPacket, financialPacket, qualitativePacket. The local Skill's preflight must pass before this template is invoked.

Four parallel reviews run per row: business model & circle of competence, moat & management, financial quality, valuation with margin of safety. Each review emits a JSON object inside ```json ... ``` fences.

The local Skill applies evidence audit (source_ref must resolve into the input, source_value must match the atomic value), hard vetos (9 rules), deterministic ranking, and an auditable Markdown report.
Research aid only. The Skill never produces target prices, position sizes, or buy/sell instructions.
